title: Greece's €3.5 Billion Relief Package · 15 Sep
keywords: Greece, cost of living, inflation, relief package, election politics, fiscal policy, Eurostat, Bank of Greece, household income, EU economic governance, primary surplus, Athens, pensions, tax cuts
notes: The Greek government is rolling out a €3.5 billion tax-and-wage relief plan it says households deserve after years of austerity and rising prices. Critics, however, see a politically timed manoeuvre ahead of the 2027 elections, and inflation data suggest the cost-of-living squeeze is far from over. The debate touches on a wider European question: how do governments translate macroeconomic success into relief that citizens actually feel?
